name: Amazon WorkSpaces Personal (Windows)

modes.label: AlwaysOn monthly bundle (licence included, us-east-1)
modes.commit_note: Flat monthly per desktop regardless of use. Not prorated except in the first month: deleting a desktop mid-month still bills the full month. Switching from AlwaysOn to AutoStop takes effect the next month. Bundle/volume changes are prorated per day.
modes.note: Official AWS WorkSpaces price JSON (us-east-1, 'Windows <bundle> AlwaysOn Billed by the month Included'), cheapest storage option root 80 GB + user 10 GB (GP bundles 175+100 GB). More storage raises the monthly price (e.g. Standard 80/50 = $35). Windows desktop experience on Windows Server; licence included.

modes.label: AutoStop: monthly fee + hourly (licence included, us-east-1)
modes.note: Hourly rate plus a fixed monthly fee per desktop ($7.25 at 80+10 GB, $9.75 at 80+50, $13 at 80+100, $19 at 175+100). The fee is charged even if the desktop never runs. Partial hours are billed as a full hour (official). AutoStop stops the desktop only after the AutoStop Time following DISCONNECT. That time defaults to 60 min and is configurable only in 60-minute steps, so every session pays at least one extra idle hour unless the caller stops the desktop via the StopWorkspaces API. Resume takes typically under 90 s. GPU and GeneralPurpose bundles do not hibernate on AutoStop, so in-memory state is lost (disk is kept). Stopped desktops pay only the monthly fee; switch to AlwaysOn above the break-even (Power: ~92 h/month).

modes.label: AlwaysOn monthly bundle, Ubuntu Linux (us-east-1)
modes.note: Ubuntu (22.04/24.04) bundles, root 80 GB + user 10 GB. Amazon Linux bundles are $2/month cheaper (Value $21, Standard $29, Performance $41, Power $66, PowerPro $123). RHEL is +$1 over Amazon Linux-ish (Standard $32) and Rocky Standard is $30. Ubuntu GeneralPurpose 16/64 $284 and 32/128 $568 exist only in us-east-2 and ap-southeast-5 in the price JSON.

modes.label: AutoStop: monthly fee + hourly, Ubuntu Linux (us-east-1)
modes.note: Same mechanics as the Windows AutoStop mode: partial hours are billed as full hours, there is a 60-min default idle tail after disconnect, and the fixed monthly fee is charged even if the desktop is never used. Amazon Linux hourly is $0.17/0.26/0.43/0.64/1.49.

modes.label: AlwaysOn GPU bundles, Windows licence included (us-east-1)
modes.note: The GPU quota for every Graphics bundle defaults to 0 per Region, so a quota ticket is required. AutoStop variants: g6f.large $20/month + $0.54/h, g4dn $22 + $1.54/h, g6.xlarge $20 + $1.80/h, g7.2xlarge $38.46 + $5.77/h (JSON shows $42.14 fee for us-east-1). G7 is only in us-east-1/us-east-2/us-west-2. No hibernation on AutoStop for GPU bundles. Full list (Gr6, g6.8x/16x, g7.4x-12x) is in raw/aws-workspaces-daas-pricing.txt.

plans.name: AWS account (no plan fee)
plans.note: Per-desktop pricing. Simple AD and AD Connector are included in WorkSpaces pricing. Only AWS Managed Microsoft AD costs extra. Requires an AWS Paid account plan (card on file).

free.note: WorkSpaces Free Tier (once per account, new to WorkSpaces, starts at first launch and lasts 3 billing cycles). 2 Standard AutoStop WorkSpaces of any OS, 40 h combined per month. Plus 5 Performance AutoStop Ubuntu WorkSpaces, 100 h combined per month. The monthly infrastructure fee is waived. Unused hours do not roll over. Requires an AWS Paid plan (card).

knobs.label: Region
knobs.why: WorkSpaces prices differ by region. Factors are Windows Power AlwaysOn (80+10 GB) vs us-east-1 from the official price JSON (publication 2026-09-28). Ratios vary by bundle: Frankfurt Standard is x1.12, Power x1.21. AutoStop fees also rise (EU Frankfurt $9, Tokyo $10).

caveats: CORRECTION vs sweep: Standard 2 vCPU/4 GB is $33/mo AlwaysOn (not $31) and $7.25/mo + $0.30/h AutoStop (not $0.28/h), per AWS's official WorkSpaces price JSON fetched 2026-09-28.
AutoStop monthly fee (month_fee_per_instance) is not an engine field: add $7.25 (or $9.75/$19 for bigger storage) per desktop per month by hand.
No 4 vCPU / 8 GB bundle: 4 vCPU needs Power (16 GB).
Provisioning takes ~20+ min; AutoStop resume ~1-2 min; seat/desktop-oriented DaaS, not an API sandbox. No agent API.
Office/Visual Studio application bundles, BYOL Windows 10/11 and WorkSpaces Pools/Core not encoded.
Network egress for streaming is included; internet egress from the VPC (NAT etc.) is normal AWS data transfer, not encoded (null).

Not encoded: (1) Windows BYOL, $4 cheaper per month on the small bundles (Value $21, Standard $29, Performance $41, Power $66, PowerPro $123, GP $272/$544 AlwaysOn; hourly $0.17/0.26/0.43/0.64/1.49/2.20/4.40). It requires a minimum of 50 WorkSpaces per Region per month (GPU: 4 AlwaysOn or 20 AutoStop) on dedicated hardware, enabled via account manager or ticket, with a 6-month grace period. (2) WorkSpaces Pools: closed to new customers since July 31, 2026. (3) WorkSpaces Core bundles: BYOL-only, via a VDI partner. (4) Office/Visio/Project/Visual Studio add-ons ($8.77-$304.15/month), charged monthly even on AutoStop.

fleet.verification: Personal details, email and phone; payment card may be required.
fleet.notes: Default quota is 1 WorkSpace per Region (adjustable). GeneralPurpose.4xlarge/8xlarge: 1 each. Every Graphics bundle (g4dn, g6*, gr6*, g6f*, g7*): 0. Standby: 5. Custom images: 40. WorkSpaces API throttling: 2 calls per second. You can resize up only once per 6 h and down once per 30 days. Use Service Quotas to request increases; applied quota and regional availability must be checked.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When the WorkSpaces support hibernation, the state of the desktop is saved to the root volume of the WorkSpace. The WorkSpace resumes when a user logs in. All open documents and running programs return to their saved state
snapshot_auto.note: AutoStop running mode only: triggered by the AutoStop timeout after disconnect (default 1 h) or a manual Stop; hibernation includes memory (running programs). Not for GPU bundles, GeneralPurpose.4xlarge/8xlarge, or Windows Server 2025 / Win11 24H2+ with nested virtualization. AlwaysOn never stops. Separately, automatic root+user volume snapshots every 12 h are used for Restore/Rebuild (scheduled backups, not this feature).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: If you've launched a Windows or Linux WorkSpace and have customized it, you can create a custom image and custom bundles from that WorkSpace.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Only as an image capture (CreateWorkspaceImage): disk only, root/OS volume ('A custom image contains only the OS, software, and settings'), no memory, no user volume; new WorkSpaces boot from it via a custom bundle (template). No user-triggered checkpoint of a specific WorkSpace: Restore/Rebuild only use the automatic 12-hourly snapshots.

harness_api.note: WorkSpaces API covers desktop lifecycle, images, bundles, IP groups, directories and pools only; no agent/harness operations. Seat-oriented DaaS.

egress_allowlist.quote: you must ensure that the security group for your WorkSpaces allows outbound traffic on ports 80 (HTTP) and 443 (HTTPS) to all destinations (0.0.0.0/0)
egress_allowlist.note: WorkSpaces sit in your VPC: security groups on the WorkSpace ENI (IP/CIDR/port egress rules), NACLs, and no-internet by omitting NAT/public IP. Domain-level via AWS Network Firewall domain-list rule groups ('You can create allow lists and deny lists with domain names', network-firewall docs) or Route 53 DNS Firewall in the same VPC; separately billed AWS services, not WorkSpaces settings.

ingress_rules.quote: An IP access control group acts as a virtual firewall that controls the IP addresses from which users are allowed to access their WorkSpaces.
ingress_rules.note: IP access control groups (CIDR allowlist for streaming clients, up to 30 rules/group), plus VPC security-group inbound rules on the WorkSpace ENI; no public app ports by default (streaming gateway only).

guest_firewall.note: Full VM (Windows Server-based desktop or Amazon Linux/Ubuntu/Rocky/RHEL) with its own kernel; with local admin/sudo, Windows Defender Firewall or iptables/nftables work. Not stated in docs.

secret_proxy.note: No credential-injection proxy in WorkSpaces; credentials live inside the desktop (user/AD login). Not documented either way; false derived from the product scope and API surface.

volume_attach.quote: WorkSpace root and user volumes come in set groups that can't be changed.
volume_attach.note: Storage is fixed to one root + one user volume, each resizable up to 2000 GB (increase only). No extra EBS/network volume attach feature.
